plain.li: The wind's swung round, and it smells wet.
The frogs are calling, so there's rain coming.
[spacer] Rain's coming, and there's no weather control out here to stop it.

warm.li: Rain's coming, so I'll bring your washing in with mine.

cheerful.li: Rain's coming, and I'm going to stand out in it.

gloomy.li: Rain again, and I've only just dried out.

cold.li: Rain coming, so the outdoor work goes first.

plain.li: Look at those clouds stacking up, there's a storm in them.
[!lowtech] Check the conduits, there's a storm on the way.

warm.li: Stay in if you can, there's a storm on the way.

cheerful.li: There's a storm coming, and I love the sound of it on the roof.

gloomy.li: Storm coming, and lightning always finds something to burn.

cold.li: A storm's coming, so keep away from the tall trees.

plain.li: The wind's gone round to the north, it'll snow.
[lowtech] Bank the fires well, snow's coming.
[!lowtech] Check the heaters, there's snow coming.

warm.li: Snow's coming, so wrap up warm, all of you.

blunt.li: Snow soon, so finish the outside work.

cheerful.li: Snow's coming, proper snow by the look of it.

gloomy.li: Snow's coming, and it'll be ankle-deep in the fields.

cold.li: Snow coming, and the hunting will be harder in it.

plain.li: The low ground's already gone white, fog's coming up.

warm.li: Fog's coming, so stay where we can see you.

blunt.li: Fog soon, stay close to the walls.

cheerful.li: Fog's coming, it'll make the trees look like ghosts.

gloomy.li: Fog's coming, and it always feels like something's in it.

cold.li: Fog coming, so the watch won't see far.

plain.li: Not a cloud anywhere, it'll stay fine.
The dew's heavy on the grass, so it'll be fine.

warm.li: Fine weather coming, we'll get the washing dry at last.

blunt.li: Fair weather, so no excuses for the outside work.

cheerful.li: Sun's coming, and I've already picked my spot to sit in it.

gloomy.li: Fine weather coming, and it'll rain the day we harvest anyway.

cold.li: Clear weather ahead, so the hunters can go out.

plain.li: Gray coming in from the west, and staying, by the look of it.

warm.li: Gray weather coming, good for staying in with a story.

cheerful.li: Cloud's coming, it'll be cooler for the work.

gloomy.li: No sun again, I expect.

cold.li: [!lowtech] Overcast coming, so the solar panels will be slow.

plain.li: The grass is all leaning one way, wind's on its way.
[!lowtech] Good wind coming, the turbines will spin fast.

warm.li: Wind's coming, put a warm layer on before you go out.

blunt.li: Wind coming, weigh down anything light.

cheerful.li: Windy weather coming, good for drying the washing.

gloomy.li: Wind's coming, it'll blow the heat right out of the rooms.

cold.li: Strong wind coming, the fires will need more fuel.

plain.li: The air's gone gritty already, dust's on the way.

warm.li: Dust's coming, wet a cloth for your face.

cheerful.li: Dust coming, so it's a day for indoor work.

gloomy.li: Dust's coming, and it'll be in the beds for days.

cold.li: Dust coming, keep the doors closed.

plain.li: I'd have bet my supper on that forecast.

warm.li: I'm glad I was wrong this time.

cheerful.li: Can't win them all, the sky's a tricky one.

gloomy.li: Even the sky won't do what I say.

cold.li: My reading of the sky was off.

plain.li: The water froze in the bucket by the door.
[lowtech] Keep the fires going all night, all of you.
[!lowtech] Check the heaters, every one of them.

warm.li: Sleep close together and share the blankets until this breaks.

cheerful.li: Well, at least it's a record.

cold.li: Keep your hands covered, frostbite's the danger now.

plain.li: Drink before you're thirsty, all of you.
[lowtech] Wet cloths on your necks, and work in the shade.
[!lowtech] The coolers can barely keep up with this.

warm.li: Take it slow today, I don't want anyone collapsing.

cheerful.li: Hot enough to cook on a rock, I'd bet.

gloomy.li: The crops won't take much more of this.

cold.li: Work at dawn and dusk, not in this.

plain.li: The paths are mud from here to the fields.
Everything smells damp, even the bedding.

warm.li: Come in and get those wet things off.

gloomy.li: My boots haven't been dry in a week.

cold.li: The low ground will flood if this goes on.

plain.li: The topsoil blows off the fields in clouds.

warm.li: Water the young plants first, they feel it most.

cheerful.li: Good drying weather, if nothing else.

cold.li: If it doesn't rain soon, we lose the crop.

plain.li: Strange weather for the season, but I won't complain.
[winter] Water's dripping off the roofs in the middle of winter.

warm.li: Let's have supper outside if it holds.

cheerful.li: Coats off, everyone, it's practically summer.

gloomy.li: The ground'll freeze again overnight, you'll see.

cold.li: Use it for the outside work while it lasts.

plain.li: I felt that one in my teeth.

warm.li: Stay close to me until it passes.

cheerful.li: That one lit up the whole sky!

cold.li: It's further off than it sounds.

plain.li: It's coming down thicker now.
The tracks from this morning are gone already.
We'll be shoveling paths before long.

warm.li: Look at it on the fence posts, like little caps.
Stand here with me a minute, it's lovely.

blunt.li: Pretty, and a nuisance by morning.

cheerful.li: Fresh snow, and not a footprint in it yet.

gloomy.li: There goes the last of the green.

cold.li: Heavy flakes, so it'll settle.

plain.li: Close your eyes and you could be anywhere.
[summer] Too hot by noon, but this early it's just right.

warm.li: Come and sit, there's room in the sun for two.

cheerful.li: I'm not moving until the shadow gets me.

gloomy.li: My knees are older than they were last summer.

cold.li: The warmth loosens the joints, that's all.

plain.li: First light, and the birds already at it.
[winter] The frost's going pink in the light.

blunt.li: Sun's up, so the day's on.

cheerful.li: Morning, everything, it's a good one.

plain.li: That little brown one always comes last.
[fall] Getting fat for the cold, are you?

warm.li: Slow down, there's enough for all of you.

blunt.li: Eat and go, I've work to do.

cold.li: They know where the scraps go, that's all.

plain.li: This one sits in the palm just right.
[lowtech] Good flint, this, I'll knock an edge on it later.

cheerful.li: This one looks like a face, see the eyes?

cold.li: Mostly worthless, but this one has a vein of something.

plain.li: Crumbs under the table again.

cheerful.li: Nearly done, and then it'll shine.

cold.li: Dirt spreads sickness, so it goes.

plain.li: Something's been at the bark on that one.

cheerful.li: Rabbits all along the edge, look.

cold.li: No tracks I don't know, that's what matters.

plain.li: Many happy returns, {OTHER_nameDef}.

gloomy.li: Another year older, {OTHER_nameDef}, same as the rest of us.

cold.li: Happy birthday, {OTHER_nameDef}, I've marked the day.

plain.li: You've got straw all through your coat again.

warm.li: There's a good one, steady now.

cheerful.li: Who's getting fat on our scraps, then?

gloomy.li: You don't care what day it is, do you.

plain.li: All right, {PET_nameDef}, but stay out from under my feet.

warm.li: Good company, you are, {PET_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: Look who's following me about again.

gloomy.li: You'll get bored of me soon enough.

cold.li: Stay close and stay quiet.

plain.li: It's bouncing off the roof like gravel.

warm.li: Get under here with me.

gloomy.li: That's the seedlings flattened.

cold.li: Hail never lasts long, wait it out.

plain.li: Count heads, all of you.

warm.li: You were brave out there, every one of you.

blunt.li: Wounded inside first, then the rest.

cheerful.li: We're still here, and they're not.

gloomy.li: I keep seeing their faces.

cold.li: Count our losses, then theirs.

plain.li: Keep them out of the crops, {PET_nameDef}, that's all I ask.
[first] Somebody had to go first, {PET_nameDef}, and it's you.
[line] It runs in the family, {PET_nameDef}.
[new] New blood at the front, {PET_nameDef}, let's see what you make of it.

warm.li: They trust you, {PET_nameDef}, so look after them.
[line] The old one would be proud of you, {PET_nameDef}.

cheerful.li: Look at you out in front, {PET_nameDef}!
[first] The very first to lead them, {PET_nameDef}, how about that.

gloomy.li: Don't lead them anywhere bad, {PET_nameDef}.
[line] The old one's gone, {PET_nameDef}, and it's down to you now.

cold.li: You lead because the others let you, {PET_nameDef}.
[new] The strongest leads, {PET_nameDef}, and that's you for now.

plain.li: {PET_nameDef}'s about again, keeping its distance.
Somebody tell the others {PET_nameDef}'s back.
[grazer] {PET_nameDef}'s eating our grass again, the cheek of it.
[predator] Keep the animals close, {PET_nameDef}'s out.

warm.li: There you are, {PET_nameDef}, safe another day.
[grazer] Leave {PET_nameDef} be, it's doing no harm.

cheerful.li: Hello, {PET_nameDef}, nice of you to drop by.
[grazer] {PET_nameDef}'s getting fat on our meadow.

gloomy.li: {PET_nameDef}'s still out there, still watching us.
[grazer] One hard winter and {PET_nameDef} won't come back.

cold.li: {PET_nameDef} is getting too close to the fields.
[grazer] {PET_nameDef} would feed us for a week.
